newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - April 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - April 2.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page on Wednesday:

* The White House said top advisers and friends of President Clinton helped find a lucrative job for Webster Hubbell, a friend of Clinton's who was facing a criminal investigation after leaving the Justice Department.
* Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu scheduled a visit to Washington to meet with President Clinton as violence escalated in the Middle East.
* The Dow Jones industrial average, rose 27.57 points to close at 6,611.05, steadying after a two-day slide.
* Big car rental companies have stopped letting people rent cars just using a Visa Check card or the similar Master Money Card, causing ire among card companies that issue them.
* The Presbyterian Church in the United States said a majority of its regional bodies made a policy against ordaining practising homosexuals into church law.

* Russian President Boris Yeltsin has made a 37-year-old former physicist, anti-nuclear activist and market reformer first deputy Prime Minister in the hope he can ease the country's shift to capitalism.
* An arbitrator appointed by the U.S. Supreme Court recommended that Ellis Island be divided between New York and New Jersey, drawing the line where New Jersey wanted it.
